disposition_reason: Table 1 prints calcium, magnesium, zinc and copper (mg/L) for 14 raw and processed cow, sheep and goat milks from Sarajevo, including 0.9% and 1.5% fat cow milk; lead, cadmium, iron, manganese and nickel were below flame AAS detection limits in all samples.

study.design: Small survey of farm and market milk
study.origin: local farms in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina (raw milk); processed milk origin not stated
study.method: Dry ashing of 1 mL at 550 °C, dissolution in 3 mol/L HCl; flame AAS (Varian AA240FS)
study.qa: Spike recoveries 84-109% for all metals in four milk samples; no CRM

controls.control: milk fat level of processed cow milk
controls.outcome: Zn <LOD (0.9% and 2.8% sterilized) vs 7.00-13.00 mg/L (2.8-3.8% pasteurized); authors report Ca, Mg and Zn rising with fat (r > 0.600)

unresolved: Zinc values up to 22.31 mg/L in lactose-free milk are about five times typical milk zinc; kept as printed.
Lead LOD (1.091 mg/L) is about 50 times the EU lead limit for milk, so the non-detects carry little information.
Fat content was taken from packaging; raw milk fat not determined.

regulatory_or_exposure.value: 200 mL milk per day, 60 kg body weight
